review_note: Keep diary method and partial mediation; shorten the explanation of how responsiveness qualifies the depth scale.

edits.before: Week 9's depth scale says how far a turn goes. It has no field for whether the turn landed, and this is the paper that says the missing field is where the work happens: the same disclosure, received two different ways, is two different interactions. The emotion-over-facts result is the one that changes the advice. A step up the scale need not mean a more private subject — it can be the subject you were already on, with how you felt about it attached. That is a cheaper move than the scale implies, and it is available to someone who would rather not hand over a more private fact.
edits.after: Week 9's depth scale does not record responsiveness. This paper is one reason to check how a disclosure was received as well as how private it was. A step up need not introduce a more private subject: it can add how you felt about the subject you were already discussing.
edits.reason: Keep the missing dimension and concrete alternative; remove repeated declarations of significance and the unmeasured claim that the move is cheaper.
